key_insight: A guided diffusion model can reconstruct physically realistic bubbly-flow velocity fields from phase-limited 2D measurements, including the difficult bubble phase.
engineering_relevance: This offers a generative-prior approach for recovering sparse or inaccessible multiphase flow data, which is useful for experiments, diagnostics, and data assimilation in turbulent bubbly flows.
method: Train on 2D slices extracted from fully resolved 3D DNS of buoyancy-driven bubbly pseudo-turbulence
Use a guided diffusion model to generate velocity fields unconditionally or conditioned on surrounding liquid-flow information
Patch adjacent reconstructed slices to approximate 3D flow inside a bubble
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the reconstructed bubble-phase velocity field reproduces key statistical features and that patched 2D slices give a reasonable 3D reconstruction inside a bubble.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on DNS-derived 2D slices and simple slice patching, so robustness to noisy experimental measurements and strongly different flow regimes remains to be validated.
paper_title: Gappy Reconstruction of Bubbly Flows by Guided Diffusion Models
